subject: Leonida (GTA 6)
title: Is Leonida a real place? GTA 6's fictional Florida, explained
answer: No. Leonida is a fictional U.S. state created by Rockstar Games for Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is based on Florida. Its main city, Vice City, is the series' long-running version of Miami. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on Nov. 19, 2026.
body:
Rockstar has named several regions of Leonida. Vice City is billed as the "sun and fun capital" of America. The Leonida Keys are a tropical island chain that resembles the Florida Keys, and Grassrivers is a swampy area that appears modeled on the Everglades. Port Gellhorn is described as Leonida's forgotten coast of cheap motels and closed-down attractions, Ambrosia is home to a sugar refinery and a local biker gang, and Mount Kalaga sits on the state's northern border.

The name follows the series' habit of renaming real places: GTA V's San Andreas is a fictional version of Southern California, and Los Santos stands in for Los Angeles. Vice City first appeared in the original Grand Theft Auto in 1997 and was the setting of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City in 2002.

Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, reaffirmed the Nov. 19, 2026, release date during an investor call in May 2026.
in_the_news: Grand Theft Auto VI, set in the fictional state of Leonida, is scheduled for release on Nov. 19, 2026.

faq.q: What state is Leonida based on?
faq.a: Florida. Vice City is based on Miami.

faq.q: Is Vice City a real city?
faq.a: No. It is Rockstar's fictional version of Miami.

faq.q: What are the regions of Leonida?
faq.a: Rockstar has shown Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga.
Take-Two says Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Nov. 19, 2026.
